basis: Fuel-derived kiln carbon per tonne clinker in the 2025 public-SI illustration

fuel_conversion_assumptions.off_spec_policy: UOP jet-focused design with light-olefin recycling and separate diesel, naphtha and residual streams
fuel_conversion_assumptions.carbon_mass_fraction_status: Representative composition assumptions, not UOP measurements. Distinct from carbon-to-jet yield.
fuel_conversion_assumptions.coproduct_scaling: Diesel and naphtha masses per kg pure methanol use their Table 2 output divided by 1200 * 0.9985. Jet alone is recalculated at the user-selected 85% carbon yield. This adapted slate is not an exact UOP plant reproduction.
fuel_conversion_assumptions.coproduct_use_policy: User-approved fuel use: diesel and naphtha fully combust one year after production. Matching avoided upstream fossil production and combustion CO2 are credited in the production year. No petrochemical naphtha pool or allocation.

coproduct_combustion.counterfactual_basis: Equal-mass, composition-equivalent fossil fuel. The existing representative carbon mass fraction (0.85) applies to both synthetic and displaced fuel; this is a webinar equivalence assumption, not a measured fuel specification.

fuel_conversion_assumptions.residual_policy: User-approved aggregate closure: upstream methanol residual and methanol-to-X residual are released as non-fossil CO2 in the production year. This is a webinar modelling assumption, not a quantified fate reported by UOP. No heat credit.
fuel_conversion_assumptions.uop_process_boundary: Methanol feed through olefin production, concentration and fractionation, oligomerization, hydrogenation and product fractionation. Upstream CO2-to-methanol synthesis is outside this patent model.
fuel_conversion_assumptions.uop_recycle: Unconverted ethylene and propylene return to olefin concentration/fractionation. C4-C8 olefins recycle to oligomerization. Internal recycle is not an additional carbon input or a substitution credit.

fuel_conversion_assumptions.residual_heat_credit_status: No credit pending a quantified process energy balance, not an assertion that heat recovery is absent
release_blockers: Rebase operating energy and hydrogen to the recycled multi-output design
fuel_conversion_assumptions.status: user-selected literature-supported candidate design, incomplete for LCIA release
fuel_conversion_assumptions.interpretation: 85% is methanol carbon retained in jet. Diesel and naphtha are additional physical products drawn from the remaining carbon. The balance remainder stays explicit. This is a simulation-informed assumption, not measured industrial performance.

methanol_source: JRC99380 Sections 3.4 and 4.1, Table 2; approved standalone process replaces SI.2 methanol intensities
assumptions: SI.2 capture/storage intensities and approved JRC99380 methanol synthesis are applied to the 2025 fuel-derived streams. This is not a full 2025 plant inventory.
SI.2 implies 5% liquefaction loss and 1.44% transport/boil-off loss of loaded CO2 on this route. SI.1 prose instead mentions 3% injection loss. Do not combine them or silently equate them.
Permanent storage has no later leakage in the central webinar scenario.
85% methanol-carbon-to-jet yield is user-selected and informed by the UOP simulation. Product carbon mass fractions of 85% are separate representative composition assumptions, not measured yields.
Diesel and naphtha masses follow UOP Table 2 per kg pure methanol, corrected for the reported 99.85% feed purity. The jet yield is independently set to 85%, not the source 85.4%.

The methanol-stage residual and conversion residual exclude all product carbon. User-approved aggregate closure releases both as non-fossil CO2 in the production year, with no heat credit. This is a webinar assumption, not a quantified UOP fate. Historical residual field names refer to amounts before this closure, not additional terminal pools.
Diesel and naphtha combust one year after production. Equal-mass fossil production and combustion are credited in the production year, without allocation.
Jet carbon is counted as product at production and released at combustion one year later, never counted twice in the same balance.
Avoided fossil jet production/combustion is a substitution credit, not a physical sink for the captured carbon.
Calcination, capture-boiler carbon and wider upstream emissions are outside the quantified fuel-carbon ledger. Their physical routes remain on the diagram.
Published GWP results and internal engineering quantities are not used in this diagram. The shared fuel trajectory follows published SI.2; scientific release remains separately gated.
